summary: Ephemeral accept-queue flood from async embedding retransmit causing API 5xx cascade
description: Issue summary: At ~2026-03-13T14:22Z we observed a sustained surge of 5xx responses from the API gateway for QuantEase tenant during an embedding upload. The gateway reported accept-queue growth leading to upstream runtime errors and a cascade of retries. Impact: customer reports ~35% of embedding requests returning 502/503 and elevated latencies for unrelated traffic for ~25 minutes. Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated pool (tenant id qte-9922). Observed behaviour: accept-queue depth on edge proxies increased rapidly, ephemeral proxy keepalive exhaustion, upstream serving-runtime CPU threads spiking and frequent runtime restarts. Expected behaviour: short-lived spikes handled by autoscaler and backpressure without customer-visible 5xx floor.
impact: Customer-facing: QuantEase observed failed embedding uploads and downstream application retries. Business impact: batch ingestion job for search indexing failed, delayed production sync. Platform impact: transient elevated 5xx floor across several routes in the same dedicated pool; internal SLOs degraded during the window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer performed an async bulk embedding upload split into ~4k small chunks with client-side aggressive retries on 429/timeout. 2) Several clients retried in parallel (concurrent clients ~80). 3) Gateway accept-queue filled with half-open connections from ephemeral proxies. 4) Serving runtime started shedding connections and returning 502/503 under pressure. Note: replication attempt in staging with smaller load reproduced accept-queue growth within 2 minutes.
logs: Edge proxy logs: repeated 'accept queue full' entries at 2026-03-13T14:23:02Z; apigw metrics: accept_queue_length increased from 5 -> 320 within 3 minutes; runtime logs: 'watchdog: worker restart due to thread pool saturation' and 'kvcache lock contention' around 14:25Z. Example stack traces and truncated logs linked in related_confluence_pages. -- Request IDs: r-qte-14f3, r-qte-14f7, r-qte-15a2.
investigation_notes: Hypotheses: (a) customer-side retry storm amplified by partially successful chunk uploads leading to retransmit hot loop; (b) ephemeral proxy keepalive depletion prevented normal connection reuse, increasing accept queue; (c) kvcache prefetch thrash in dedicated serving runtime caused increased CPU and runtime restarts. What we checked: - Ingress metrics, accept queue histograms, proxy keepalive pool size (saw slots approaching zero). - Tenant telemetry (concurrent streams and active connections spiked). - Serving runtime thread and GPU metrics show CPU-bound scheduling spikes prior to OOMs. Partial findings: a correlated pattern of small embedding chunks with HTTP/2 streams re-opened on retries; many retransmits within 200-800ms. Linked to an older client library that uses exponential backoff with capped jitter that in practice created synchronized retry waves. Cross-references: see SUP-314159 for similar accept-queue patterns during bulk embedding traffic.

resolution: Workaround applied: tenant-level short-term throttling for small-blob embedding route and increased ephemeral proxy keepalive capacity on affected nodes. Outcome: 5xx rate returned to baseline within 10 minutes. Permanent fixes planned: 1) Add a server-side adaptive ingress-shedder that detects retransmit amplification and applies queuing/backoff for high-frequency small-chunk uploads. 2) Improve runtime kvcache locking to avoid prefetch lock amplification during high churn. 3) Customer guidance: update SDK to v2.4.1 which includes jittered exponential backoff and reduced chunk concurrency. Rollout notes: Ingress shedder design will be prototyped in staging (ticket INT-1202), runtime kv fix targeted for next minor (runtime) release. Postmortem scheduled on 2026-03-18; action owner list will be added to the incident RCA.
postmortem_followup: Owners: Miguel Torres (ingress mitigations), Leo Nguyen (runtime fix), Priya Rao (SRE operational runbook). Tasks: SDK outreach, automated detection rule, increase default proxy keepalive threshold for dedicated pools, KPI monitors for accept-queue growth. Target completion: 2026-03-31.
additional_context: This incident highlights interaction between customer client behavior (aggressive retries + small chunking) and platform connection handling. Recommend adding more tenant-specific telemetry to detect retransmit amplification earlier.
notes_for_support: When contacting the customer: recommend using updated SDK with fixed backoff, suggest batching strategy changes (larger chunk sizes, lower concurrency). If similar spike observed, apply temporary tenant priority-shed and throttle small-blob embedding route while notifying runtime on-call.
